objects.economic_definition: Economic cost required to obtain one consistently defined unit of useful technology performance.
objects.point_in_time_semantics: Value is available only from the first public observation timestamp.
objects.revision_semantics: Revisions create a new vintage; prior vintages remain reproducible.

objects.economic_definition: Versioned definition and measured quantity of useful technology performance used as the denominator for cost/performance.
objects.point_in_time_semantics: Definition/version is frozen as known at the observation timestamp.
objects.revision_semantics: Breaking unit-definition changes require a new version bridge, not silent restatement.

objects.economic_definition: Distinct active adopters/users/organizations meeting a declared activity threshold during the measurement period.
objects.point_in_time_semantics: Use the count and activity definition first published for the period.

objects.economic_definition: Defensible denominator of entities that could adopt the technology under the declared use case and geography.
objects.point_in_time_semantics: Use denominator definition available at cutoff.
objects.revision_semantics: Denominator redefinitions are versioned and never backfilled silently.

objects.economic_definition: Deduplicated count of documents or utterances containing the version-pinned narrative concept during the period.
objects.point_in_time_semantics: Only documents available by timestamp are countable.
objects.revision_semantics: Topic-model relabeling requires a model-versioned recomputation lineage.

objects.economic_definition: Count of distinct eligible sources actively mentioning the narrative during the period.
objects.point_in_time_semantics: Source universe is versioned at cutoff.
objects.revision_semantics: Source additions/removals create a new universe version.

objects.economic_definition: Deduplicated count of version-pinned mentions explicitly opposing, falsifying or reversing the focal narrative.
objects.point_in_time_semantics: Only text and stance model available at cutoff may be used.

objects.economic_definition: Company revenue attributable to the declared market/segment using the accounting definition available at publication time.
objects.point_in_time_semantics: Available on original report/publication date.

objects.economic_definition: Aggregate revenue of the version-pinned industry universe for the same economic scope as company revenue.
objects.point_in_time_semantics: Use industry constituents and estimates known at cutoff.
objects.revision_semantics: Universe or estimate revisions are vintaged.

objects.economic_definition: Effective deliverable capacity of the declared bottleneck after known operational constraints.
objects.point_in_time_semantics: Use capacity known or guided at cutoff.
objects.revision_semantics: Capacity guidance/estimates are vintaged by publication date.

objects.economic_definition: Demand for the bottleneck in the same unit/scope as effective supply capacity.
objects.point_in_time_semantics: Use orders/usage/forecast vintage known at cutoff and label observed versus estimated demand.

objects.economic_definition: Total or price return of a version-pinned tradable asset over a declared interval.
objects.point_in_time_semantics: Computed only from prices observable by cutoff.
objects.revision_semantics: Corporate-action corrections are versioned; original raw observations remain auditable.

objects.economic_definition: Realized variability of returns over a declared backward-looking PIT window.
objects.point_in_time_semantics: Uses only returns available through cutoff.

objects.economic_definition: Decline from the prior PIT running peak of the declared asset/portfolio price series.
objects.point_in_time_semantics: Running peak and current value use only information through cutoff.

objects.economic_definition: Observable transaction/mark price of the declared financial instrument at the analysis timestamp.
objects.point_in_time_semantics: Use contemporaneous bid/ask/last with quote timestamp.

objects.economic_definition: Implied volatility derived from contemporaneous option prices under a version-pinned inversion convention.
objects.point_in_time_semantics: Derived only from contemporaneous option quotes and contract terms.

objects.economic_definition: Cash flow available to capital providers under a version-pinned definition derived from PIT financial statements.
objects.point_in_time_semantics: Available only from the original financial report date.

objects.economic_definition: PIT growth rate of company revenue over a declared comparable period.
objects.point_in_time_semantics: Uses financial statement vintages available at cutoff.

objects.economic_definition: Operating income divided by revenue under the accounting definitions available at publication time.
objects.point_in_time_semantics: Available on original report date.

objects.economic_definition: Market value of operating assets implied by equity value plus net debt and other declared capital claims at the analysis timestamp.
objects.point_in_time_semantics: Market components and latest available balance-sheet components are PIT aligned.
objects.revision_semantics: Balance-sheet restatements are vintaged; market prices are timestamped.

objects.economic_definition: Self-financing portfolio net asset value at the declared timestamp after recognized cash flows and costs.
objects.point_in_time_semantics: Uses positions and marks available at cutoff.
objects.revision_semantics: Corrections require an auditable restatement event.

objects.economic_definition: Change in self-financing portfolio NAV over a declared interval with external cash flows handled by a version-pinned convention.
objects.point_in_time_semantics: Computed from NAV values available through cutoff.

objects.economic_definition: Value of assets convertible to cash inside the declared liquidity horizon under stated haircut assumptions.
objects.point_in_time_semantics: Positions, prices and liquidity assumptions are those known at cutoff.
objects.revision_semantics: Haircut methodology changes require version pin.

objects.economic_definition: Sum of absolute economic exposures before netting, under a version-pinned exposure convention.
objects.point_in_time_semantics: Uses positions and prices available at cutoff.

objects.economic_definition: Decline of portfolio NAV from its prior PIT running peak.
objects.point_in_time_semantics: Peak and current NAV use only information through cutoff.
objects.revision_semantics: NAV restatements create a new drawdown vintage.
